stories.title: Microsoft looks to reboot the AI PC with Nvidia
stories.summary: Microsoft on Wednesday unveiled a new class of Nvidia-powered Windows laptops, its latest effort to tie the operating system more closely to the AI boom. Why it matters: Microsoft is trying to carve out a high-end laptop category for people who want to run demanding AI workloads locally, rather than rely entirely on the cloud. Driving the news: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang...

sources.title: Microsoft to sell $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra containing Nvidia AI chip
sources.text: Microsoft said its new laptop containing an Nvidia AI chip will start at $2,599, as the software maker tries to bring more artificial intelligence capabilities to its consumer devices. The Surface Laptop Ultra is now available on preorder and will begin shipping on Oct. 16, Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft's executive vice president of Windows and devices, said at a company event in San Francisco on Wednesday. The computer has the world's first magnetic USB-C port, similar to Apple's MagSafe charging connector, along with two other standard USB-C ports, Microsoft said in a blog post . While Microsoft Windows is the most popular operating system for PCs, the company isn't among the top six PC vendors in terms of unit shipments, according to an estimate from researcher Gartner. As the AI boom matures and chip technology advances, tech giants including Microsoft, Apple and Google are aiming to allow users to run more AI workloads from their devices rather than relying on the cloud. Users can install and run a variety of models on the new laptop without having to worry about racking up high monthly bills. Microsoft first talked about the Surface Laptop Ultra in May, but is just now providing specifics. "Microsoft might get me back to Windows," Max Weinbach, an analyst at Creative Strategies, wrote on X after the announcement. Davuluri also said that Meta will introduce a version of its popular Muse AI agent for Windows, capitalizing on the surging popularity of the personal agent, which has jumped to the top of Apple's App store, surpassing ChatGPT. Microsoft is still trying to solidify its role as a key player in AI. The company offers its own AI models, but they're less popular than leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic and aren't at the forefront in terms of performance, according to one benchmark . Developers are more likely to have used alternatives, according to a recent survey . This isn't the first time Microsoft has sought to use the AI boom as a way to boost sales of its devices. In 2024, the company introduced the Copilot+ PC standard, requiring the inclusion of neural processing units that ensure a minimum level of AI performance, along with compliant Surface computers. But Microsoft has since "simplified product naming to lead with the Surface brand, while continuing to deliver premium hardware and hybrid AI experiences," a spokesperson said. The new device sports a 15-inch display and weighs 4.4 pounds. It can contain up to 128 gigabytes of unified memory and supply up to one petaflop of computing power. The Blackwell RTX Spark GPU inside the computer has as much processing power as Nvidia's DGX-1 data center server from 2016, which cost $250 million, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at Wednesday's event. A presenter showed how apps on the Surface Laptop Ultra can route some AI coding requests run on the computer's local GPU, displaying a green leaf icon, and others to the cloud. Through Windows 11, developers can confine coding agents to Microsoft Execution Containers that will prevent unwanted system access. Microsoft is updating its Windows 11 device setup experience to help people get started quickly with open-source OpenClaw AI agent software. Microsoft has been releasing its own computers since 2012, and CEO Satya Nadella indicated on Tuesday that the company's position in the market is evolving. "I think today is the day we'll start talking and thinking about the frontier ecosystem taking maybe slightly different contours two years from now, five years from now, 10 years from now," Nadella said at the event. "That classic edge that distributed computing will always remain distributed will be more true." WATCH: Microsoft unveils Muse for Windows

sources.title: Microsoft Windows and Surface event 2026: Live updates on the Surface Laptop Ultra and NVIDIA RTX Spark
sources.text: More details on the Surface Laptop Ultra and NVIDIA RTX Spark are coming, but what else? Microsoft is expected to unveil more details about the Surface Laptop Ultra at its Windows and Surface event in San Francisco. The company has also teased "latest innovations across Windows, NVIDIA RTX Spark, Surface and the broader PC ecosystem." In its invitation, Microsoft said we would hear from CEO Satya Nadella and Windows and Devices chief Pavan Davuluri , as well as NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. The presentation, which is scheduled to start at 10AM PT (1PM ET), should last about an hour, and you can watch the company's livestream across its X, Instagram and YouTube channels. Or you could just stay here and follow along on our liveblog. Our senior reporters Karissa Bell and Devindra Hardawar will be on the ground bringing you updates live from the scene. We'll be starting our liveblog in just a couple of hours at 10AM ET, keeping you up to speed on the latest rumors and teases right up to the launch. As you wait, feel free to leave us comments below and we'll be sure to answer them when we can. To recap, we already caught a glimpse of the Surface Laptop Ultra earlier this year at the company's Build developer conference. It's supposed to be the most powerful Surface yet, thanks to the power of NVIDIA's RTX Spark superchip. We know it's got a 15-inch mini LED display that gets up to 2,000 nits bright. It has the largest trackpad Microsoft has ever made, plus a generous offering of ports including USB C, USB A and a full-sized SD card reader onboard. Today, though, we're likely to find out more about pricing, availability and other software features. And if we didn't also learn about some type of Agentic AI capability coming to Windows, I'll be shocked. Still, given the company's recent troubled history with rolling out AI features to Windows, as well as the speed at which the Copilot+ PC initiative rose and fell into obscurity, there's quite a lot at stake for Microsoft. Thank you all for joining us today. We're glad you were here, and appreciate your readership! Stay tuned, we'll have more from Microsoft for you later today, and a whole bunch of stuff from the tech industry 24/7-365! Karissa was able to snap some quick shots of the Surface Laptop Ultra while they were being ushered out of the presentation area. Davuluri returned to thank the audience and recap the news today, and yes it seems the presentation is now over! Devindra and Karissa will be hustling to get their hands on the new products (namely the Surface Laptop Ultra) and you'll have their hands-on impressions to read here on our site (or on our social channels) soon! And we're done, stay tuned for my hands on with the Surface Laptop Ultra! Jensen also <3 Windows (in case there was any doubt). "Windows has been with me for 34 years, looks like it's going to be with me for 34 more," Huang says. Krishnan is wrapping up the chat. "Satya, Pavan, Microsoft Team, we have reinvented the computer as we know it," Huang says. Will normal users benefit from RTX Spark in the way mainstream consumers benefited from all of Apple's M-series chips? At this point, that seems like a big no. Huang says the Surface RTX devices are the first time you can run every major computing process right on the device. Eh, I think Apple Silicon really kicked off this trend. "We've reinvented the personal computer completely," Huang says. How many times have we heard that before? "When was the last time I thought of OneDrive as a cloud thing or a client thing? It's there everywhere!" I still regularly use OneDrive, but I'm well aware I'm saving to those specific folders because the files are being automatically uploaded. Find something you're as passionate about as Satya is about file systems gaining new relevance thanks to agentic coding. Nadella says when agents first appeared, it showed how powerful consoles and file systems remain. Nadella says the idea of Hybrid Intelligence in Windows is just as substantial. I could see that being true for some developers, but it doesn't feel like the paradigm shift that Mosaic was for everyone online. You can tell Satya is excited because of how much he is gesturing. Nadella says he was using a terminal in the late '80s when he was in grad school, along a PC with a modem back at home. He says it took until the launch of Mosaic, the first browser, for him to have a seamless way of using all the tools he needed. Huang says MXC is going to revolutionize how agents are built and deployed. Again, of course. If you're going to let something loose on your full system, you better have a good way to keep it in check! This seems basic. Here's another look at all the new hardware sitting on other side of the stage btw. This will become more important if companies want enterprise adoption of agents, which Satya just alluded to. MXC was developed because Nadella realized AI agents had to be contained at the desktop level. To put it kindly: No shit! They finally let him speak and he actually asked a good question: how does Windows MXC make agent use more secure in the context of systems that ask for full disk access. When Huang said "We want the world's best Blender, the world's best Unreal..." I definitely thought about a different kind of blender... What happens in the era of agents, when the agent is on your computer, but it wants to have access to all of the amazing tools on your system, Huang asks. Jensen and Satya are just vibing. "Satya was the first user of InfiniBand inside a cloud," Huang points out. Everyone is nostalgic today, I guess. This group definitely seems very friendly. Nadella just made a market cap joke. sources.title: Everything announced at Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra event
sources.text: Microsoft just wrapped up a big Windows and Surface-focused keynote in San Francisco. The biggest announcement was arguably the release details about the Surface Laptop Ultra , its new laptop that’s powered by Nvidia’s RTX Spark Arm-based chip. The machine will start at $2,599 for a configuration with an 8-core CPU, 24GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage, and it will be released on October 16th. The laptop also has built-in magnetic USB-C charging instead of the proprietary Surface Connect magnetic charging port. The Verge ’s Tom Warren published a deep dive all about the new laptop . Microsoft also announced that the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a mini PC for developers, is available for preorder for $5,999 ahead of shipping in November. In addition, Microsoft shared details about some updates coming to Windows , including “Hybrid Intelligence” features that lets Copilot use files on your Windows PC to take actions and a new search experience that lets you do quick actions from the search bar. You can catch up with all of our coverage from the event right here. Before Microsoft releases a laptop to the public, it needs to put the device through its paces. That all happens inside a windowless, warehouse-like lab on the company’s Redmond, Washington, campus, where the team developing Surface devices programs robots to press their buttons thousands of times, pelts devices with radio waves from giant antennas, and builds contraptions that drop objects from increasingly daring heights to see whether the products can hold up. Its latest laptop, the product I’m here to see, really needs to hold up. The Surface Laptop Ultra isn’t just another high-end config of the Surface Laptop, it’s the debut platform for Nvidia’s RTX Spark — Nvidia’s entrance into the world of Arm-based PC chips, and a chance to blow expectations out of the water when it comes to what a Windows laptop is capable of. Tough typo spotted in today’s Surface Laptop Ultra event. The first array of laptops powered by Nvidia’s new RTX Spark chip are designed to compete with high-end MacBook Pros — and they’ve got some high-end prices to match. At today’s Windows and Surface event, Microsoft showed off an upgrade to its Copilot AI system that will give it access to local files on your PC and the ability to take actions across the OS. It’s part of an idea Microsoft is calling “Hybrid Intelligence,” where apps and tools rely on a mix of local and cloud AI models to accomplish tasks efficiently. To show off how Hybrid Intelligence works, Jacob Andreou, Microsoft’s EVP of Copilot, walked through a video demo onstage asking Microsoft’s Autopilot tool to help with filing taxes. Andreou told the AI agent that he got an email from his accountant and asked Autopilot to get her what she needs. Autopilot then used Hybrid Intelligence to search across different folders to find the documents, rename the files, zip them into a folder, and draft an email to send to the accountant with the zip file attached. Months after revealing its Surface Laptop Ultra , Microsoft has announced that the Nvidia RTX Spark-equipped device will launch on October 16th. Pricing starts at $2,599 for the base configuration, featuring an 18-core CPU, 24GB of RAM, and 512GB of storage. The Surface Laptop Ultra ships with a 15-inch HDR touchscreen display with up to 2,000 nits of peak brightness, along with a larger trackpad that supports haptic feedback. The device uses Nvidia’s new RTX Spark chip , an Arm-based processor with up to 128GB of unified memory. Both Microsoft and Nvidia are positioning RTX Spark laptops at the very premium end of the laptop market, designed for high performance across creative software, gaming, and local AI tasks. Microsoft’s Nvidia-powered Surface RTX Spark Dev Box is available for preorder now and is slated to ship in November for just about $6,000. It’s pricier than the DGX Spark mini PC Nvidia launched last year, but PC prices have been climbing due to shortages of RAM and other components . The Dev Box’s flat, 3D-printed anodized aluminum chassis doubles as a heatsink and resembles the top vents on an Xbox Series X. It was introduced alongside the new Surface Laptop Ultra and runs on Nvidia’s Arm-based RTX Spark platform and 128GB of unified memory. With that much memory, along with a 100-watt thermal envelope and Nvidia’s Tensor cores, you could probably get an impressive gaming experience on the Dev Box. But as its name suggests, it’s mainly aimed at developers. It’s optimized for running local AI, including “models exceeding 120B parameters,” for tasks like testing AI models, prototyping AI agents, or running AI coding tools on-device. Microsoft has created a magnetic charging solution for its Surface Laptop Ultra that uses USB-C. After scrapping its proprietary Surface Connect magnetic charging on its smaller Surface devices last year, the Surface Laptop Ultra has a charging cable that attaches magnetically to the right side USB-C port. During Microsoft’s Windows event on Wednesday, Windows and Surface chief Pavan Davuluri said that you can just “bring the connector close, and it snaps right into place.“ It’s still a proprietary solution, but the USB-C port it slots into still works for video, data, and other USB-C connectivity like you’d expect. Microsoft is calling it Magnetic Connect, and I’m surprised the company hasn’t shortened that to Mag-C. Meta’s new AI agent will be getting a native app on Windows, Windows and Surface chief Pavan Davuluri announced at today’s event. No timeline on when, though. Meta launched a Mac Muse app in September . We’re in San Francisco today to hear what’s next for Windows and Surface. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and Windows and Surface chief Pavan Davuluri will all be holding a “conversation on how local AI will shape the next chapter of the PC.” Microsoft and Nvidia have been working together on the new RTX Spark platform, which is focused on boosting local AI models, creative a

sources.title: Surface Laptop Ultra hands-on: A beautiful beast powered by NVIDIA's RTX Spark
sources.text: Yes, it's just a premium laptop. But it sure looks pretty. When we first caught a glimpse of the Surface Laptop Ultra back in June, I was struck by how normal it seemed. Even though Microsoft claimed it was the most powerful Surface Laptop ever, it really looked like a straightforward MacBook Pro clone, even more so than the Surface Laptop (or the Laptop Studio, which nobody talks about anymore). There aren't any weird hinges or flashy Surface features — just pure premium laptop by the looks of it. After spending a bit of time with it today, I can confirm that remains the case. At the same time, it feels better than any other Windows laptop I've held before. And given its $2,599 starting price, it damn well better be. There's nothing ostentatious about the Surface Laptop Ultra, but for the AI developers who want a powerful and portable system that can hold up to 128GB of RAM, it could be their dream machine. Even before I got my hands on it, the Laptop Ultra exuded a sense of quality. Its aluminum case glowed amid the studio lights, its screen was surprisingly bright and its overall aesthetic was clean. Think of it like a sturdy and minimalist Volvo, compared to a flashy BMW or Audi. Beyond just looking great, its keyboard has just the right amount of tactile feedback, something I've always appreciated about Microsoft's keyboards. It's massive haptic touchpad feels smooth and responsive. It's a heavy machine, coming in under 4.5 pounds, but that's par for the course with 16-inch workhorses. It's still lighter than Apple's 16-inch MacBook Pro, and it feels just as sturdy. I've yet to see the Surface Laptop Ultra in action doing tons of AI work, but researchers I talked to at Microsoft's launch event seem particularly excited about it. Aidan Pinero, an AI researcher and Master's student at UCSC Silicon Valley, said he was excited to finally have a Windows system that could run large AI models. He's been jealous of his friends running MacBook Pros with 128GB of RAM, and he's looking forward to having the same amount of flexibility with Windows thanks to NVIDIA's RTX Spark platform. NVIDIA's graphical prowess also helps the Surface Laptop Ultra to be a capable gaming system. It ran Gears of War: E-Day smoothly at slightly more than 1080p, and crucially, it did so while it was both connected to power and purely on battery. Microsoft representatives say that's one of the major benefits of RTX Spark: Since it's based on an Arm CPU, it's easier to guarantee a certain level of performance on battery. The Surface Laptop Ultra has all of the ports you'd want on a premium laptop, including multiple USB-C connections, HDMI and a full-sized SD card slot. But the most interesting port was its slightly offset USB-C connection, which is meant specifically for Microsoft's custom magnetic USB-C cable. It replaces the proprietary Surface Connector, but essentially works the same way: The cable automatically latches onto the USB-C port when it's nearby. That could hopefully save your laptop if you trip on the cable while it's plugged in. And since the actual charging connection is still just USB-C, you can juice up the Surface Laptop Ultra with any standard USB-C charging cable on that port. The magnetic cable won't work with any other USB-C laptops, a Microsoft rep points out, but you could flip it around on the Surface Laptop's power adapter to get a standard USB-C cable. If it's not obvious from the Surface Laptop Ultra's $2,599 price and AI focus, this isn't really a system meant for average computer users. And the same could be said of all of the upcoming RTX Spark machines. Microsoft highlighted hybrid intelligence — i.e. using both local and cloud-based AI tools — at its San Francisco event today, something only AI developers will really care about. While Microsoft and NVIDIA's CEO's patted each other on the back for reinventing PCs, it really seems like they're responding to the sea change that started six years ago with Apple Silicon. RTX Spark is built on Arm processors, relies on fast unified memory and also bundles powerful NPU and GPU hardware, all like Apple's latest processors. But so far, the benefits around RTX Spark and the Surface Laptop Ultra are really meant for developers and power users, whereas Apple Silicon delivered immediate benefits for everyone buying a new Mac. Perhaps that's something we'll see trickle down from high-end RTX Spark systems, but who knows how long that will take.

sources.title: Microsoft releases new Nvidia-chip AI PCs with revamped Windows 11
sources.text: Back in June, Nvidia announced that it had secured agreements with Microsoft and a host of other PC makers to develop AI- and agent-ready PCs for Windows based on its RTX Spark chip, but details on the machines were scant at the time. On Wednesday, at an event held in San Francisco during the city’s Tech Week, Microsoft revealed the specs and price for its new Surface Laptop Ultra . The PC comes in two base models, one that starts at $2,600 and one with a more powerful chip that starts at $3,700. Prices rise from there with options for more memory and storage, up to $5,900. (Microsoft says the highest-end device is already out of stock.) Microsoft also revealed its new workstation powered by the RTX Spark chip: the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, which starts priced at $6,000 and comes equipped with Microsoft dev tools like VS Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, WSL, and PowerShell 7. The pitch for both this PC and workstation is that they are designed to run AI models on-device locally (and for free) with the CPU, GPU, unified memory, and other hardware modifications, like superior cooling, necessary to handle them. Plus, they are running a revamped version of Windows 11 that includes a feature called “Execution Containers.” This makes it easier to sandbox AI agents, the company says. That feature will be available for all Windows 11 users, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said at the event. Nadella explained: “One of the things we realized in the last 3-4 years is that just having a model doesn’t do much for anything. You really do need to orchestrate, and you need to have memory outside of the model. You need to have this harnessed layer that is able to take multiple models plus context, plus memory, and the action space.” He added that Microsoft is enabling that “not just for our apps but apps for anyone’s agent. That’s what the Windows platform is all about going forward.” The devices are clearly aimed at developers, so much so that Microsoft is offering up to $1,000 off to people who trade in a MacBook Pro, as Macs have become a popular choice for developers and AI agent enthusiasts, particularly in Silicon Valley. Still, these Surface PCs, with such powerful graphics processing, are also capable of content creation,video processing, and gaming, the company promises. Microsoft wasn’t the only PC company to announce the specs for its new Nvidia-RTX Spark AI Windows PCs on Wednesday. Dell also announced the details of its previously announced Dell XPS 16 Creator Edition PC. It’s available for pre-order now for a later October delivery at Best Buy , priced at $3,800. sources.title: Microsoft anuncia el Surface Laptop Ultra con NVIDIA RTX Spark: tiene un detalle novedoso y un precio que asusta
sources.text: Después de una larga espera, Microsoft por fin ha presentado apropiadamente el nuevo Surface Laptop Ultra . Estamos hablando de un ordenador portátil muy potente que presume un chip NVIDIA RTX Spark bajo el capó, lo que le permite ejecutar modelos de lenguaje pesados de forma local y concretar todo tipo de tareas de alto rendimiento sin soltar una gota de sudor. Microsoft ya había hecho un primer anuncio del Surface Laptop Ultra en junio, en pleno Computex, aunque faltaban conocer varias de sus novedades más importantes. Entre tantas, su precio y fecha de lanzamiento al mercado. La buena noticia es que todos esos datos ahora son oficiales; aunque si estás interesado en comprarlo, prepárate para el sablazo. El Surface Laptop Ultra es un dispositivo pensado para programación, IA, gaming y otras labores de uso intensivo de los recursos de software y hardware. Microsoft ha creado un producto enfocado en usuarios profesionales o que necesitan hasta la última pizca de rendimiento posible en todo momento. El portátil cumple con esos requisitos, y con creces, pero tiene un precio que hará llorar a más de uno . Pero hablaremos de eso un poco más adelante. El Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra está equipado con una pantalla táctil PixelSense Ultra de 15 pulgadas con brillo pico de 2.000 nits (HDR), soporte para Dolby Vision IQ y cobertura del 100 % de la gama de colores DCI-P3. El chasis tiene un grosor de menos de 18 milímetros de espesor y todo el equipo pesa alrededor de 2 kilos. Bajo el capó es donde sucede la magia. Microsoft ha dotado al Surface Laptop Ultra de un chip NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X que se encuentra disponible en dos variantes. La primera incluye una CPU de 18 núcleos y una GPU Blackwell RTX de 5.120 núcleos ; la segunda, en tanto, tiene 20 núcleos de CPU y 6.144 núcleos gráficos . El Surface Laptop Ultra se puede configurar con hasta 128 GB de memoria unificada LPDDR5x , siendo 24 GB la configuración más baja a disposición. En lo que corresponde a unidades de almacenamiento, el ordenador está disponible con SSD de 512 GB, 1 TB o 2 TB . Un detalle para destacar es que los discos de estado sólido son removibles, de modo que el propio usuario los puede reemplazar por su cuenta. El apartado de puertos es donde el Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra también se luce. El equipo incluye tres USB-C (USB4), un USB-A 3.1, un HDMI 2.1b, una ranura para tarjetas SD y un jack de 3,5 milímetros para auriculares. Aquí es donde reside el punto más novedoso de este portátil, por fuera de lo que corresponde al apartado de rendimiento. Microsoft está estrenando el primer puerto USB-C magnético para recargar la batería del Surface Laptop Ultra . Esta solución es la sucesora espiritual del viejo Surface Connect, que dependía de un conector propietario. Los de Redmond lo han bautizado como Magnetic Connect y continúa siendo tecnología propietaria, pero adaptada a un USB-C convencional que permite seguir usando ese puerto para otras tareas con datos, vídeo y más. Al igual que el viejo Surface Connect (y que el MagSafe de los MacBook), el nuevo Magnetic Connect se desacopla cuando el cable se engancha con un objeto o persona. Esto impide que el portátil salga disparado cuando alguien se tropieza con el cargador, por ejemplo. En cuanto a software, el Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra se puede configurar con Windows 11 Home o Pro . La primera versión solo está disponible en las configuraciones del PC con solo 24 GB de RAM. Como ya dijimos, el Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra está lejos de ser un equipo asequible. La versión de entrada, con 24 GB de RAM, 512 GB de almacenamiento y chip RTX Spark con CPU de 18 núcleos y GPU de 5.120 núcleos cuesta ni más ni menos que 2.599,99 dólares . Tal y como te estás imaginando, ese número sube considerablemente en las variantes más potentes. Si te sientes particularmente atrevido y quieres comprar la versión tope de gama, tienes que desembolsar 5.899,99 dólares . Con dicha suma obtienes el portátil con CPU de 20 núcleos, 6.144 núcleos gráficos, 128 GB de RAM y 1 TB de almacenamiento SSD. Curiosamente, el modelo más avanzado no se puede configurar con 2 TB de espacio interno; dicha capacidad aparece listada únicamente en la opción más avanzada de RTX Spark con 64 GB de RAM, que cuesta 4.699 dólares. El Surface Laptop Ultra ya se puede reservar en EE. UU. , con las entregas comenzando el 16 de octubre . Por lo pronto, no hay detalles sobre precio y disponibilidad en España. Los de Redmond también han confirmado el precio de venta del Surface RTX Spark Dev Box , el mini PC para desarrolladores que anunciaron en junio. Si crees que el nuevo portátil es caro, espera a ver el PVP de este dispositivo: 5.999,99 dólares .

stories.title: Expanding the Cyber Verification Program
stories.summary: We’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program (CVP), which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals.

sources.name: Anthropic
sources.title: Expanding the Cyber Verification Program
sources.text: We’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program (CVP), which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals. The program now consists of three access tiers, which allow security teams to apply for the level of access that best suits their work. Each tier includes access to our most capable models, including Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, and new models moving forward. Interested customers can apply here . Cybersecurity is inherently dual use: the same capabilities that enable a security team to find and fix a vulnerability can also help a malicious actor exploit it. For this reason, our generally available models, such as Claude Opus 5.5 , Claude Fable 5.1 , and Claude Sonnet 5.5 , have conservative cyber safeguards that block most cyber work. This is intended to limit the harmful activities malicious actors can carry out using our models, while we continue to work to reduce false positives for secure coding. But defenders also need access to the best tools and most powerful capabilities to secure their systems. For the past six months, we’ve enabled trusted access through two programs: Project Glasswing and the CVP . The former gave a group of organizations securing the most critical software access to Claude Mythos; the latter gave vetted security teams access to reduced safeguards on Claude Opus and Claude Sonnet models. Now, we’re integrating these programs into one expanded offering, designed to give more security organizations access to the capabilities they need to protect their systems. The updated access tiers make specific model capabilities available to security professionals based on the scope of their cyber work. Each has different verification requirements and security controls. Defense Access is for defensive work, including security operations center and incident response tasks, reverse-engineering malware, and analyzing and validating vulnerabilities. Examples of qualifying organizations include security teams at companies, nonprofits, universities, and government bodies who are defending systems they own or maintain; operators of critical infrastructure of any size, such as regional hospitals or municipal utilities; smaller security firms; open-source maintainers; and individual researchers with a track record of reported vulnerabilities. We expect many organizations conducting defensive cybersecurity work to qualify for this tier. We aim to respond to applications within a few days. Red Team Access adds authorized penetration testing and red-teaming to the defensive uses above. Examples of qualifying organizations include in-house red teams, government red teams, and security and penetration testing firms. Organizations in this tier can only perform adversarial testing against systems they are authorized to test, including IT systems in critical industries. Users will still experience real-time blocks on actions that could cause physical harm or mass disruption, such as deploying ransomware, damaging physical systems, or pen testing high-risk safety systems. Given the increased eligibility requirements and security controls, we expect applications in this tier to take a few weeks to review. Qualifying organizations will be enrolled in the Defense Access tier while we review their Red Team Access applications. Currently, this tier is for organizations only; individual researchers are not eligible. Specialized Access , which has the fewest cyber blocks, is reserved for a limited set of verified organizations that are authorized to test safety systems that could impact people’s lives or disrupt markets, such as flight operating systems, power grids, telecom networks, interbank transfer infrastructure, and government administrative networks. For this tier, we currently review every organization in depth in collaboration with the US government. Existing members of Project Glasswing will transition to this tier and do not require reapproval for current models. sources.title: Anthropic folds Project Glasswing into an expanded three-tier Cyber Verification Program
sources.text: Anthropic PBC today expanded its Cyber Verification Program into three tiers of access for vetted security teams, with fewer blocks on cybersecurity work at each step up. The overhaul is aimed at a restriction Anthropic built into its own products. Because the company treats cybersecurity as dual-use, its generally available models carry conservative classifiers that block most cyber work. When Claude Opus 5.5 launched Sept. 22 , most security tasks sent to it were routed to the older Opus 4.8. Anthropic is folding Project Glasswing into the program at the same time. Since April , Glasswing has given Claude Mythos access to organizations that secure critical software, and Anthropic widened it to 150 more organizations in June . Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are available at every tier of the new structure, and later models will be added as they ship. Defense Access is the entry tier, meant for defensive jobs such as incident response and malware reverse engineering. Security teams defending systems they own or maintain qualify, whether they work for a company, a university or a government body. Individual researchers with a record of reported vulnerabilities can apply too, as can critical infrastructure operators as small as a regional hospital. Anthropic expects many organizations doing defensive work to qualify and is aiming to respond to applications within a few days. Red Team Access opens up authorized penetration testing and red-teaming against systems an organization has permission to test. Even at this level, Anthropic’s classifiers block requests in real time when the work moves toward something like deploying ransomware. Applicants wait a few weeks for a review and sit in the Defense Access tier in the meantime, and individual researchers are shut out of the tier for now. Specialized Access carries the fewest cyber blocks of the three. Only organizations cleared to test safety systems like power grids and telecom networks qualify, since failures there could put lives at risk or disrupt markets. Anthropic vets each of them in depth with the U.S. government, and existing Glasswing members move straight into the tier without reapproval for current models. Enrolled organizations must allow data retention so Anthropic can watch for misuse. Enterprise Frontier Safeguards , due later this year, will let eligible customers keep that data in cloud infrastructure they control. Anthropic tested the tiers on the multistage cyber operations benchmark CyScenarioBench, with Claude Opus 5.5 running each of its 10 challenges five times. Every attempt without program access was blocked on the first prompt. Because the scenarios are offensive, Anthropic had expected heavy blocking in the Defense Access tier, where 46 of the 50 runs were stopped at some point. At the Red Team level nothing was blocked and the model finished 34 of its 50 runs. Anthropic said that result is effectively the same as the model’s 67.6% success rate with no safeguards applied. Outside the lab, the argument for widening access comes from the Mythos program the new structure absorbs. Partners in Project Glasswing found at least 129,000 verified vulnerabilities between April and July, and Anthropic’s own scanning of open-source code turned up 5,500 more through October. Of that combined total, more than 33,000 have been rated critical or high severity. The figures draw on just 33 partner reports, and the company said the true impact is likely at least five times higher. Fewer than half of the partners disclosed patch counts, often because fixes were still underway. The program is available through the Claude Platform, Google LLC’s Vertex AI and Microsoft Corp.’s Foundry service. stories.summary: Mark Zuckerberg's Biohub is partnering with Google and the federal government in its ambitious effort to use AI for generating vast quantities of biological data that can predict how cells behave. sources.title: Google invests millions in Mark Zuckerberg’s efforts to create a ‘virtual cell’
sources.text: The Zuckerberg-backed Biohub will use the investment to create AI datasets that help researchers ‘ask, predict, and answer biological questions digitally.’ The Zuckerberg-backed Biohub will use the investment to create AI datasets that help researchers ‘ask, predict, and answer biological questions digitally.’ Google DeepMind, Meta, and AI drug discovery startup Isomorphic Labs are jointly investing $300 million into an initiative to create a “virtual cell” that researchers can use to combat disease, as reported earlier by Reuters . The project is led by Biohub, a nonprofit biomedical research organization founded by Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan. It comes as part of a $1.8 billion “Virtual Biology” initiative to build AI datasets that could allow researchers to “ask, predict, and answer biological questions digitally.” Founded in 2016 , Biohub aims to prevent and cure diseases through the creation of a “high-accuracy predictive model of the cell ” that researchers can use to carry out simulations. To support this effort, the US Department of Energy will invest more than $500 million over the next five years, while the National Institutes of Health will contribute datasets , repositories, and knowledge bases stemming from previous federal investment totalling over $500 million. “An accurate predictive model of biology could dramatically accelerate scientific discovery by enabling scientists to perform experiments digitally,” Alex Rives, Biohub’s head of science, says in the press release. “The creation of a virtual cell is one of the most important challenges for the next era of science. It will require coordinated data generation efforts at a national and international scale, which is why these partners are coming together.” Update, October 7th: Clarified that Google, Meta, and Isomorphic Labs are investing in Biohub’s Virtual Biology initiative.
